info.title: incident.io API V2 (baton-incident-io connector surface)
info.description:
Describes only the endpoints baton-incident-io calls. Scope is derived from pkg/client/client.go; response shapes are derived from the structs in pkg/client/model.go and settled against incident.io's published OpenAPI 3.0 document at https://api.incident.io/v1/openapiV3.json (accessed 2026-09-29), which covers the V2 endpoints despite the v1 path.

Only the properties the connector's structs declare are modelled. incident.io's document describes many more per resource -- UserWithRolesV2 alone adds is_active, seats, slack_user_id and the deprecated role field, and ScheduleV2 adds timezone, team_ids, permalink, created_at, updated_at, annotations, next_shifts and holidays_public_config. The omissions are deliberate -- spec scope is connector scope.

Paths are written relative to the connector's own base, which is the constant baseDomain = "https://api.incident.io/v2" in pkg/client/client.go, with segments appended by url.JoinPath. incident.io's own document instead uses https://api.incident.io as the server and spells these paths /v2/users, /v2/users/{id} and /v2/schedules; the two are equivalent.

Auth: an incident.io API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer` by uhttp.WithBearerToken. The connector sets Content-Type and Accept to application/json on every request, including the GETs.

Pagination: cursor-based. The connector sends `page_size` (its own default of 100 when the caller passes 0) and `after`, then replays `pagination_meta.after` from the response as the next `after`. `after` is omitted entirely when empty, so the first request carries only `page_size`. An empty `after` in the response ends the sync.

servers.description: Hardcoded as baseDomain in pkg/client/client.go. The connector exposes no override for it.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: incident.io users and the RBAC roles attached to them.

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description: On-call schedules, their rotations, and their current shifts.

get.description:
Called by pkg/client/client.go ListUsers. Backs three syncers at once: the user syncer builds one user resource per record, and the base-role and custom-role syncers derive their entire resource sets from the roles embedded in these records -- incident.io exposes no standalone roles endpoint, so pkg/connector/base_roles.go and custom_roles.go deduplicate roles by id across the user list.

The connector sends neither the `email`, `slack_user_id`, nor `include_inactive` filters that incident.io supports, so deactivated users are excluded by the API default. Those parameters are omitted here because spec scope is connector scope.

200.description: A page of users, each with its roles inlined.

get.description: Called by pkg/client/client.go GetUser from the user syncer's Grants, to read one user's base role and custom roles and emit the corresponding role grants. Note the envelope differs from the list endpoint: a single `user` object, not a `users` array, and no pagination_meta.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user. The connector uses this value as the Baton user resource id and appends it with url.JoinPath.

get.description:
Called by pkg/client/client.go ListSchedules. The schedule syncer emits one resource per schedule, then reads two things off each record: `current_shifts` for who is on call right now, and `config.rotations[].users` for who is in each rotation.

incident.io documents that `next_shifts` is only populated when page_size is 25 or lower. That does not affect this connector, which requests 100 by default and never reads `next_shifts`.

apiKey.description: incident.io API key, sent by uhttp.WithBearerToken.

pageSize.name: page_size
pageSize.description: Number of records to return. The connector always sends it, substituting client.ItemsPerPage (100) whenever the caller passes 0. incident.io's own default is 25 and its maximum is 10000.

after.name: after
after.description: Cursor: the id of the last record from the previous page. The connector replays `pagination_meta.after` here, and WithQueryParam drops the parameter entirely when the value is empty -- so the first request of a sync carries no `after` at all.

Error.description: incident.io error response. The connector does not decode this body -- uhttp surfaces the status, and the connector does not branch on the payload.

UsersListResult.description: Envelope for GET /users, decoded into client.UserResponse. Modelled as written: the connector reads the array off `users` and the cursor off `pagination_meta`.

UserShowResult.description: Envelope for GET /users/{id}, decoded into client.SingleUserResponse.

SchedulesListResult.description: Envelope for GET /schedules, decoded into client.ScheduleResponse.

PaginationMeta.description: Cursor envelope, decoded into client.Meta. Only these two fields are declared by the connector.

page_size.description: The maximum number of results that was requested. Decoded but not read.

after.description: Cursor for the next page. The connector returns this as its page token; an absent or empty value terminates the sync.

PaginationMetaWithTotal.description: The schedules endpoint returns incident.io's PaginationMetaResultWithTotalV2, which adds total_record_count. The connector decodes it into the same client.Meta struct, so total_record_count is discarded; it is documented here but not modelled as read.

total_record_count.description: Present in the vendor response; not declared by the connector's struct.

User.description: incident.io's UserWithRolesV2, limited to the properties pkg/client/model.go declares. Both /users and /users/{id} return this shape.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user. Used as the Baton user resource id.

name.description: Name of the user. Used as the resource display name.

email.description: Email address of the user. Not marked required -- incident.io's document lists only id, name, role, base_role, custom_roles, seats and is_active as required, so a user without an email is possible.

base_role.description: The user's single base RBAC role. The connector treats an empty `base_role.id` as 'no base role' and skips both the resource and the grant in that case.

custom_roles.description: Additional RBAC roles. Carries omitempty in the struct, so an absent array is expected and handled.

Role.description: incident.io's RBACRoleV2. The connector uses this same struct for both base and custom roles, and builds role resources out of it -- there is no roles endpoint to enumerate them from.

id.description: Unique identifier of the RBAC role. Used as the Baton role resource id and as the deduplication key across users.

description.description: Description of the purpose for the RBAC role. Optional in incident.io's document.

slug.description: Unique human-readable slug for the RBAC role.

Schedule.description: incident.io's ScheduleV2, limited to the properties pkg/client/model.go declares.

id.description: Unique internal ID of the schedule. Used as the Baton schedule resource id.

name.description: Human readable name synced from the external provider.

current_shifts.description: Shifts that are ongoing for this schedule. Read by pkg/connector/schedules.go to emit on-call grants.

ScheduleConfig.description: Decoded into client.ScheduleConfig. Note the Go field is named Rotation (singular) but the JSON key is `rotations`.

Rotation.description: incident.io's ScheduleRotationV2, limited to the three properties the connector declares. The vendor shape also carries layers, handovers, handover_start_at, working_intervals, scheduling_mode and effective_from, none of which the connector reads.

id.description: Unique internal ID of the rotation.

name.description: Human readable name synced from the external provider.

users.description: The people in the rotation, in the order they take shifts. Read by pkg/connector/schedules.go to emit rotation membership grants.

ScheduleEntry.description: incident.io's ScheduleEntryV2, limited to the four properties the connector declares. The vendor shape also carries entry_id, fingerprint and layer_id.

rotation_id.description: If present, the rotation this entry applies to on the schedule. Optional in incident.io's document.

start_at.description: Shift start. incident.io documents this as a date-time; the connector decodes it into a plain Go string and never parses it, so no format is asserted on the connector's side.

end_at.description: Shift end. Same treatment as start_at.

ShiftUser.description: incident.io's UserV2 as embedded in shifts and rotations, limited to the three properties the connector declares. Unlike the top-level User, this shape carries no roles -- the connector pairs `id` with the user resource type to build the grant.
